questions.q: Though the President of India is not a member of either House of Parliament and does not sit in its meetings, which functionary is nevertheless an integral part of the Parliament?
questions.e: Parliament consists of the President, the Council of States and the House of the People; the President is not a member of either House but is an integral part of Parliament, because a bill passed by both Houses cannot become law without the President's assent.
w: The Vice-President is only the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha; it is the President who is an integral part of Parliament.
The Prime Minister is a member of one of the Houses and is not the third part of Parliament.
The Attorney General may speak in either House without voting but is not a part of Parliament.

concepts.description: The strength, composition and sources of members of the Rajya Sabha and the Lok Sabha.
concepts.idea: Parliament is the President plus two Houses whose members come from different sources.
concepts.rule: Parliament consists of the President, the Council of States and the House of the People; the President is an integral part though not a member. The Rajya Sabha has a maximum of 250 (238 elected indirectly, 12 nominated) and at present 245: 225 states, 8 union territories, 12 nominated; seats follow population, by single transferable vote. Only Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu & Kashmir have Rajya Sabha seats. The Lok Sabha has a maximum of 550 (530 states, 20 union territories) and at present 543 (524 and 19), directly elected; voting age was lowered to 18 by the 61st Amendment. Anglo-Indian nomination ceased on 25 January 2020 after the 104th Amendment. Seats and SC/ST reservations are fixed state-wise.
concepts.example: Of Delhi's 7 Lok Sabha seats and 3 Rajya Sabha seats, only the Lok Sabha seats are filled by direct election.

questions.q: Members of the Lok Sabha from the states are elected in single-member constituencies, each member representing a geographical area. Which electoral system does the Constitution adopt for this?
questions.a: Territorial representation, or the first-past-the-post system
o: Territorial representation, or the first-past-the-post system
Proportional representation by the single transferable vote
Proportional representation by the list system
Indirect election by an electoral college of state legislators
questions.e: The Constitution has not preferred proportional representation for the Lok Sabha; it has adopted territorial representation (first-past-the-post), with one representative from each constituency.
w: The single transferable vote is used for the Rajya Sabha, state legislative councils and the offices of President and Vice-President, not the Lok Sabha.
The list system is the other kind of proportional representation; the Constitution has not preferred proportional representation for the Lok Sabha.
Lok Sabha members are directly elected by the people on universal adult franchise.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT among the demerits of the system of proportional representation?
questions.a: It denies any representation to the smallest sections of the population
o: It denies any representation to the smallest sections of the population
It eliminates intimate contacts between voters and representatives
It does not give any scope for organising by-elections
questions.e: Proportional representation aims to give even the smallest section its due share, so denying representation is the defect of the territorial system, not a demerit of PR; the other three are listed demerits.
w: This is listed: it is highly expensive.
This is listed: it eliminates intimate contacts between voters and representatives.
This is listed: it gives no scope for by-elections.

questions.e: The 42nd Amendment froze allocation and division till the year 2000 at the 1971 level; the 84th Amendment (2001) extended the ban by 25 years, up to 2026 (the freeze runs to the first census taken after 2026).
w: The freeze was at the 1971 level, not the 1961 level.
The 1981 level was never the base of the freeze.
The 1991 population figures were used later, under the 84th Amendment, for readjustment within the states.

questions.q: Under the 104th Amendment Act of 2019, the reservation of Lok Sabha seats for scheduled castes and scheduled tribes is to last until
questions.e: The reservation, originally for ten years (upto 1960), was extended by ten years each time and now lasts until 2030 under the 104th Amendment Act of 2019.
w: 2026 is the year up to which the freeze on readjustment of seats runs (the first census after 2026); it does not govern the SC/ST reservation, which was extended by ten years to 2030.
2020 is the year upto which the Anglo-Indian nomination ran and then ceased.

questions.e: The 84th Amendment Act (2001) empowered readjustment on the 1991 census; the 87th Amendment Act (2003) replaced it by the 2001 census, without altering the number of seats of any state.

concepts.description: Constituencies, readjustment of seats, SC/ST reservation and the first-past-the-post system for the Lok Sabha.
concepts.idea: Lok Sabha seats are allotted and reserved by population, and voted by territorial representation.
concepts.rule: Seats are allotted so the seats-to-population ratio is the same for all states (except states under six million), and each state is divided so that constituencies are uniform. SC/ST seats are reserved by population ratio, until 2030 under the 104th Amendment, with no separate electorate. The Lok Sabha uses first-past-the-post in single-member constituencies; proportional representation (single transferable vote or list system) was not adopted for reasons of literacy and party multiplication.

concepts.idea: A member must meet constitutional and statutory conditions and loses the seat in listed ways.
concepts.rule: A member must be a citizen, at least 30 (Rajya Sabha) or 25 (Lok Sabha) years old, and take an oath before a person authorised by the Election Commission. Disqualifications include an office of profit, unsound mind, insolvency and foreign citizenship; the Representation of the People Act adds conviction with two or more years' imprisonment, but not preventive detention. The President decides, on the Election Commission's opinion, while defection under the Tenth Schedule is decided by the Speaker or Chairman. A person elected to both Houses must opt within 10 days, or the Rajya Sabha seat falls vacant; absence for sixty days can vacate a seat. Sitting without the oath attracts a penalty of Rs 500 a day.

concepts.idea: Business needs a quorum of one-tenth and different decisions need different majorities.

concepts.description: The Union budget: constitutional provisions, stages, cut motions, grants and the three funds.
concepts.idea: The Lok Sabha controls spending through stages from presentation to the finance bill.
concepts.rule: The 'budget' is the annual financial statement of Article 112. No demand for a grant is made without the President's recommendation, and no money leaves the Consolidated Fund except under an appropriation law. The Rajya Sabha can only discuss the budget; voting on demands is the Lok Sabha's exclusive right, and charged expenditure is not voted. Cut motions are policy (Re 1), economy and token (Rs 100). A vote on account is generally for two months and one-sixth of the estimates. The Finance Bill must be enacted within 75 days. The Consolidated Fund needs appropriation, while the Public Account and Contingency Fund are operated by executive action.

concepts.description: Parliament's functions, the Rajya Sabha's position, privileges and why Parliament is not sovereign.
concepts.idea: Parliament's wide powers are bounded by privileges on one side and constitutional limits on the other.
concepts.rule: Parliament legislates on the Union and residuary subjects and can legislate on the State List in five abnormal situations, including a Rajya Sabha resolution. Its constituent power is subject to the basic structure. The Rajya Sabha has special powers under Articles 249 and 312, can alone initiate removal of the Vice-President and can approve an emergency proclamation when the Lok Sabha is dissolved. Members cannot be arrested in civil cases during the session and 40 days before and after it. Breach of privilege is always contempt, but not conversely. Unlike the British Parliament, the Indian Parliament is limited by the written Constitution, federalism, judicial review and fundamental rights.
